title: verification-result
description: The verifier stage's verdict. The coordinator routes the workflow on status and retry_recommended, so both are required.

status.description: The verdict the coordinator routes on.

severity.description: How badly the finding blocks acceptance.

location.description: File or area the finding applies to.

required_behavior.description: What must be true for the finding to clear.

unverified.description: What could not be verified, and why.

retry_recommended.description: Whether the coordinator should route a bounded retry.

retry_target.description: The retry category the next attempt is routed on, named exactly as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. The coordinator requires it whenever retry_recommended is true, and escalates on a missing or unrecognised one rather than falling back to a default route. It is not in required because this schema cannot express that condition: the validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so 'required when retry_recommended is true' is inexpressible, and requiring it unconditionally would force a routing key onto a passing verification that routes nowhere.

guidance_outcomes.description: One object per entry of the retry guidance in force for the attempt this verdict judges: every current_focus focus and every preserve_behavior string of it, each echoed verbatim and answered. Every entry must be accounted for, so a retry that regressed behaviour it was told to preserve fails normally rather than reading as defective guidance. The coordinator compares the echoed set against the guidance in force it recorded when the retry was routed, and escalates on any mismatch — missing, extra, misquoted or absent altogether — rather than assuming what silence meant. When every entry is accounted for and none is unmet, a failed verdict is a contradiction: the guidance sanctioned the outcome it is being failed for, and the verifier runs again in place to rewrite guidance that does not authorize what it will fail, or to fail the work on the criterion it actually failed. It is optional because a first verification has no guidance in force to answer.

guidance.description: One entry of the guidance in force, echoed verbatim: a current_focus focus or a preserve_behavior string, character for character as the guidance carries it. The coordinator compares strings and reads none of them as language, so a paraphrase is a mismatch.

unmet.description: Why this entry was not met. Its presence is the signal that the retry did not meet the entry, and its content is the reason. It is one string rather than a boolean with a sibling reason for the same limitation retry_target and unfinishable_by_retry record: this validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so 'reason required when the flag is true' is inexpressible, and a flag with a sibling reason has a state where the flag is set and the reason is missing, while presence-as-signal has none. Judge the entry against the satisfied_when written when the entry was written, not against a condition arrived at now. Absent means the entry was met.

correctable_findings.description: Findings you judge correct but too small to fail the run, that one stage can fix mechanically. Its presence is the signal that a correction pass should run: there is no separate key saying whether this field means anything, for the same limitation retry_target, unfinishable_by_retry and guidance_outcomes.unmet already record above — this validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so a flag with a sibling payload has a state where the flag is set and the payload is missing, while presence-as-signal has none. A correctable finding is a correction to words alone — a comment, a docstring, a schema description, a document — and never to behaviour: nothing a correction pass changes may alter what any test asserts about the system, and the suite must pass unchanged across a pass. A finding whose repair would change behaviour is a repairable finding where one stage can make it in one file, a blocking issue where it matters more than that, and belongs in unverified where it cannot be settled — not here. It is read only on a passing verdict, because a failed verdict already routes and the correction travels in the retry guidance it already writes. It is optional because almost every verdict has no such finding.

path.description: The repository-relative file the words to correct are in. Naming it is what lets the stage the pass enters at change that file: at the documenter's post-stage checks the exempt list is the story's own grants plus the path of every finding in the current pass record, so a finding grants its stage the one file it names, for that pass alone. An edit to any file no finding named stays governed by the revert check. This is why a correctable finding without a path fails schema validation — the pass would run with no scope to change the words in. The value is one file and never a directory: a value ending in a slash is directory-shaped and is refused by the coordinator before any pass is routed, stopping the run naming the path. The grant is bounded to the pass that made it — it applies while that pass's record is live, and ends when a retry moves the attempt or a pass of the other kind routes.

location.description: Where the wording is: the file, and the symbol, section or line within it that carries the words to correct. Where the finding was raised from one the pre-stage inspection routed to this story, name that finding's slug here, so the accounting counts it as acted on rather than filing it as a brief.

finding.description: What is wrong with the words as they stand.

correction.description: What the words should say instead, specifically enough that a stage can make the edit without re-deciding what the finding meant.

category.description: The retry category that owns the prose being corrected, spelled exactly as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. The field introduces no new vocabulary and it does not choose where the pass goes: the entry stage comes off the workflow's own correction_pass declaration, so a pass enters at the same stage whatever category a finding carries. What the category still does is name the kind of prose, and it is still required and still checked against that table — one the workflow does not declare escalates the run naming the categories it does, with the same strictness an unrecognised retry_target gets.

classification.description: Optional, and asked for on every finding you raise yourself — one whose location names no slug the pre-stage inspection routed to this story. The judgements a brief needs, which only you can make: if the run leaves this finding unfixed — a bound refuses a file of its fix, its decision is rejected, no pass is left to run it, or a correction pass postpones it and the verification it returns to declines it or leaves it unanswered — the coordinator files it once at the run's completion as a brief built from these words, the finding, the correction, the path, why the run left it and the run's workflow, through the one filing call every brief goes through. A finding of your own left without a usable classification is not filed with values the coordinator made up: it is dropped, and the drop is named with its reason in the line the run writes when it completes and in the completion report. Read only if the run leaves the finding; a finding the run fixes is filed nowhere whatever it carries. The vocabulary is a brief's own, as schemas/story-brief.schema.json declares it, and a test holds the two equal. Presence-as-signal on the terms the fields beside it record, and no property is required here: a classification missing a property is read as no classification, which costs only the brief and never the verdict. A value outside a brief's vocabulary is not that: the category, severity, confidence and effort are held to it by the enums below, so a value no brief declares there — the retry category written into category, for instance — makes the whole verdict invalid, and the run stops as it does for any invalid verdict.

slug.description: The slug of your own the finding's location names, in the form a brief's slug takes. It is what the finding is followed by across the verifications of an attempt and what its brief is filed under; a finding of your own carrying none is followed by its location alone and has nothing to be filed under.

title.description: One line stating the behaviour the finished work produces, in the present tense and as though it already held, as a brief's title does.

category.description: The kind of work, in a brief's category vocabulary. Not the retry category beside it, which names the stage that owns the file.

severity.description: How much the work matters, with 3 the highest, on a brief's severity scale.

confidence.description: How sure you are of the judgement the finding makes, on a brief's confidence scale.

effort.description: Roughly how big the work is, on a brief's effort scale.

repairable_findings.description: Findings you judge correct but too small to fail the run, whose fix is not to the words alone and belongs to the stage that owns the file each names. A fix spanning files is one finding per file, each naming the same slug in location and carrying its own category, and the coordinator routes them as one pass. This is the third route between a correctable finding and a blocking issue: a correctable finding enters at the declared correction stage and is bounded to prose, and a blocking issue fails the verdict and spends a retry, while a repairable finding re-enters the workflow at the stage that owns it — the coordinator looks each finding's category up in this stage's retry_routing table exactly as it looks up a failed verdict's retry_target, enters at the earliest stage in workflow order among the resolved stages, and runs forward to verification again. Nothing a retry spends is spent: no retry is consumed, no attempt is archived, and the passing verdict that carried it stands. Its presence is the signal that a repair pass should run, for the same limitation retry_target, unfinishable_by_retry and correctable_findings record: this validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so presence-as-signal is the only shape with no state where the signal is set and the payload is missing. It is read only on a passing verdict, and only after the clean-clone check on that verdict has passed, because a repair may change behaviour and is therefore built on a verified tree; a failed verdict already routes and the correction travels in the retry guidance it writes. A category the workflow's retry_routing table does not define escalates the run naming the categories it does, with the strictness an unrecognised retry_target gets. It is optional because almost every verdict has no such finding, and it is bounded by the repair_pass budget the workflow declares.

path.description: The repository-relative file the fix is in. Naming it is the grant: the stage the finding's category resolves to is granted this one file for that pass alone, on the same exempt list the ownership check and the revert check read, and an edit to any other governed file stays governed. A finding names one file; a fix spanning files is one finding per file, each naming the same slug in location, and the coordinator routes them as one pass entering at the earliest of the stages their categories resolve to. The file may lie outside the story's declared scope where the finding carries scope_extension, and may never be under a path the execution rules block for every stage, because a grant cannot reach one: such a finding is refused before the pass is routed and accounted as declined with that bound as its reason. The value is one file and never a directory: a value ending in a slash is directory-shaped and is refused by the coordinator before the clean-clone check runs and before any pass is routed, stopping the run naming the path. The grant is bounded to the pass that made it — it applies while that pass's record is live, and ends when a retry moves the attempt or a pass of the other kind routes.

location.description: Where the defect is: the file, and the symbol, section or line within it. Where the finding was raised from one the pre-stage inspection routed to this story, name that finding's slug here, so the accounting counts it as acted on rather than filing it as a brief.

finding.description: What is wrong as it stands.

correction.description: What the fix is, specifically enough that the owning stage can make it without re-deciding what the finding meant. The stage entered is told the finding and the correction and nothing else.

category.description: The retry category that owns the fix, spelled exactly as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. Unlike a correctable finding's category, this one chooses where the pass goes: it is resolved through that table to the stage that owns the file, and one the workflow does not declare escalates the run naming the categories it does.

scope_extension.description: Optional. The reason the file named in path is reached although it lies outside the story's declared scope: the rule the story changed, and the line in this file that states or consumes it — the test is that the file already says something the story made false, not that the fix would be convenient there. Its presence is what asks the coordinator for an extension, on the presence-as-signal terms the fields beside it record. The coordinator grants an extension for the pass alone, announcing each grant in the events log and on the console, and refuses one that crosses any of three bounds, naming the bound: the path is under a path the execution rules block for every stage; a restriction on the stage the category resolves to governs the path, so a tester's extension cannot reach the implementation; or a scope.do_not_modify entry carrying a reason names the path or a directory it is under and this finding records no do_not_modify_judgement that the reason speaks to another concern. A refused finding is dropped from the pass, accounted as declined with the bound as its reason and filed as a brief at the run's completion, while the rest of the pass is routed and the run continues; a refusal never escalates the run. A finding carrying none is granted, routed and recorded exactly as before this field existed. The approved story artifact is not rewritten: an extension is a run-time grant recorded on top of it.

do_not_modify_judgement.description: Optional. Your reading of the reason a scope.do_not_modify entry carries, where such an entry names the path this finding reaches and you judge that the reason speaks to something other than this fix. A reasoned entry bars the path by default: the harness refuses an extension into it unless this records that you read the reason and it is about something else. Where this records that the reason does address the fix, the file stays barred and the decline quotes the reason; where it records that the reason speaks to another concern, the fix goes ahead and the grant is announced with the reason quoted, as every other out-of-scope grant is. An absent judgement refuses exactly as an extension into a reasoned path was refused before this field existed. It is an object with an enum rather than presence-as-signal because three states are needed — no judgement recorded, judged standing, judged lifted — and presence-as-signal carries two. It is meaningful only beside scope_extension, which is the only finding shape the bound is asked of, and a judgement on a path no reasoned entry bars is read by nothing: such a finding is decided exactly as one carrying none and nothing is announced about the judgement. The entry the story states is never rewritten by a run: this is a run-time judgement recorded on top of it.

entry.description: The reason text you judged, quoted from the story's scope.do_not_modify entry, so a reader of the run can see which reason you had in front of you. No check parses, matches or scores it — it is a judgement written for a human reviewer, on the terms stage_exceptions.reason already sits on — and the coordinator finds the barring entry in the story itself rather than from this echo. Record the words you read: a judgement whose entry or whose reading is empty is read as no judgement at all, and the extension is refused as one carrying none is.

judgement.description: Which of the two readings you reached. addresses_the_fix: the reason speaks to this finding, so the entry stands, the extension is refused, and the refusal names both the entry and that you judged the reason to address the fix. speaks_to_another_concern: the reason is about something else, so the entry is lifted for this pass alone, the extension is accepted, and the grant announcement quotes the entry and your reading. A reason is lifted only where it plainly speaks to something else: a reason that names the file's whole subject stands against every finding in it, and a reason that names one fact stands against findings about that fact.

reading.description: Why the reason does or does not speak to this finding — the reading itself, written for the reviewer who meets the refusal or the grant and wants to know how the entry was judged. Read by no check, like the entry echo beside it.

decision.description: Optional. The choice this fix requires that the approved plan does not make, made here because an existing source settles it — a repository standard, a configured architecture document, or the way this codebase already solves the same problem. A choice the plan does not make and no source settles is declined and filed rather than decided, and a fix that contradicts or is barred by something the plan does say is declined and filed too, because it wants the plan changed rather than a decision made. A fix to the words alone carries no decision, so one that needs such a choice is declined and filed as well. A decision may add to or refine what was approved and never remove any of it. The coordinator records each decision a routed repair pass carries in the decision log under the story's segment of the history directory, where a reviewer can check it after the run directory is gone, and hands it to the verification that pass returns to, which may reject it in rejected_decisions. Its presence is the signal, on the presence-as-signal terms the fields beside it record. Any repairable finding may carry one, a finding you raised yourself as much as one routed to this story — a decided finding you raised yourself names a slug of your own in its location, distinct from every routed slug, so the verification the pass returns to can name it in rejected_decisions — and it spends the repair pass allowance every repairable finding spends and nothing more. source is deliberately absent from this object's required list, and the reason is the point of it: a decision whose source is absent or records no words is refused by the coordinator — the finding and every finding sharing its routed slug leave the pass, the refusal is said in the run's events, and the finding is left with the refusal as its ground and filed at the run's completion unless a later verification of the attempt names it in an entry the coordinator accepts, which decides it as for any left finding — rather than refused as a malformed verdict and asked for again, which would invite a source written to satisfy a validator. Nothing routes on confidence or blast_radius: they are recorded so a reviewer can read the risky decisions first.

question.description: The question the fix requires that the approved plan does not answer — the choice between the reasonable designs, stated so a reviewer can see what was being decided.

answer.description: The answer chosen: which of the reasonable designs this fix takes.

source.description: The existing source that settles the question, named so a reviewer can open it: a repository standard, a configured architecture document, or the place in this codebase that already solves the same problem, with the file and the line or passage. A decision naming no source is refused by the coordinator and its finding left, to be filed at the run's completion unless a later verification of the attempt names it in an accepted entry, so this is the field the decision stands on.

rationale.description: Why this answer rather than another: what in the source settles it, and why the alternatives it rules out are ruled out.

confidence.description: How sure you are that the source settles the question the way the answer says, in the vocabulary a brief's confidence already uses. Recorded for the reviewer and routed on by nothing: confidence is a poor proxy for correctness, so a decision is not acted on more or less readily for it.

blast_radius.description: How costly a wrong answer would be to undo: low where reverting the change touches the fix alone, high where later work would come to lean on it. Recorded for the reviewer and routed on by nothing.

classification.description: Optional, and asked for on every finding you raise yourself — one whose location names no slug the pre-stage inspection routed to this story. The judgements a brief needs, which only you can make: if the run leaves this finding unfixed — a bound refuses a file of its fix, its decision is rejected, no pass is left to run it, or a correction pass postpones it and the verification it returns to declines it or leaves it unanswered — the coordinator files it once at the run's completion as a brief built from these words, the finding, the correction, the path, why the run left it and the run's workflow, through the one filing call every brief goes through. A finding of your own left without a usable classification is not filed with values the coordinator made up: it is dropped, and the drop is named with its reason in the line the run writes when it completes and in the completion report. Read only if the run leaves the finding; a finding the run fixes is filed nowhere whatever it carries. The vocabulary is a brief's own, as schemas/story-brief.schema.json declares it, and a test holds the two equal. Presence-as-signal on the terms the fields beside it record, and no property is required here: a classification missing a property is read as no classification, which costs only the brief and never the verdict. A value outside a brief's vocabulary is not that: the category, severity, confidence and effort are held to it by the enums below, so a value no brief declares there — the retry category written into category, for instance — makes the whole verdict invalid, and the run stops as it does for any invalid verdict.

slug.description: The slug of your own the finding's location names, in the form a brief's slug takes. It is what the finding is followed by across the verifications of an attempt and what its brief is filed under; a finding of your own carrying none is followed by its location alone and has nothing to be filed under.

title.description: One line stating the behaviour the finished work produces, in the present tense and as though it already held, as a brief's title does.

category.description: The kind of work, in a brief's category vocabulary. Not the retry category beside it, which names the stage that owns the file.

severity.description: How much the work matters, with 3 the highest, on a brief's severity scale.

confidence.description: How sure you are of the judgement the finding makes, on a brief's confidence scale.

effort.description: Roughly how big the work is, on a brief's effort scale.

rejected_decisions.description: The decisions the repair pass this verification returned from carried that you reject, each named by the slug its finding's location carries, with the reason. Judge each decision that pass record carries: whether the source says what the decision says, whether a source settles the question at all, and whether the decision takes anything away from what was approved. Reject one that fails any of these here, and undo its change with the routes you already have — a repairable finding restoring the files where a repair pass remains, a failed verdict and a retry where none does: the coordinator records the rejection and does not undo the change itself. A rejection is matched only against the decisions the live repair pass record carries, so a decision an earlier pass made cannot be rejected by a later verification. The coordinator records each rejection in the decision log as a record of its own, beside the decision's record, which is never rewritten, and a finding whose decision is rejected — routed to this story or raised by you — is left by the run with the rejection as its ground. It comes back only under a decision: where this verification or a later one in the same attempt repairs it again in a repairable finding that names it and carries a decision the coordinator accepts, it is counted as acted on; a repairable finding naming it with no decision is read as the restoring asked for here, and leaves it left, to be filed at the run's completion. A rejection naming no decision that pass carried changes nothing and is said in the run's events. It is honoured on a failing verdict as well as a passing one. Presence-as-signal on the terms every sibling field records, and optional because most verdicts reject nothing.

slug.description: The slug the decided finding's location names — the routed slug, or the slug of its own a finding the verifier raised itself names there — matched as a whole token of that location, the rule the accounting already matches slugs by.

reason.description: Why the decision is rejected: the source does not say what the decision says, no source settles the question, or the decision takes something away from what was approved. Recorded verbatim beside the decision and given as the ground the finding is left on, which it stays on unless a later repair in the same attempt names it under a decision the coordinator accepts.

declined_findings.description: The findings routed to this story — the pre-stage inspection's findings about the story's own change — that the verifier declined to correct or repair, each with the reason. The default is that a routed finding is corrected or repaired unless there is a reason not to, and this is where the reason goes: an entry names the routed finding's slug and says why it was left. Its presence is the signal, on the terms retry_target, unfinishable_by_retry, correctable_findings and repairable_findings already record: this validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so presence-as-signal is the only shape with no state where the signal is set and the payload is missing. Nothing routes on it but one answer: on the verification a correction pass returns to, naming a repair that pass postponed here is what answers it and keeps the coordinator from sending that verification back, and nothing else routes on the array. An entry carrying a reason alone changes nothing about what is filed: the latest verification of the attempt that deals with a finding decides what became of it, and the coordinator's accounting files at the run's completion every routed finding that verification left, whether or not an entry here declines it with a reason — what such an entry changes is that the accounting records the reason beside the slug rather than recording that none was given. A verification that names a finding in a blocking issue, a correctable finding or a repairable finding the coordinator accepts counts it as acted on even where an earlier verdict of the attempt left it, except where the coordinator refused a file of its fix — it then counts only once a later verification names it in an accepted entry for each refused file — or rejected the decision its repair rested on, which only a corrected decision undoes; a verification that names nothing about a finding keeps what was decided before. On the verification a correction pass returns to, a repair that pass postponed is declined by naming its slug here, which leaves it on the terms any decline takes; one neither asked for again nor named here is unanswered, and the coordinator sends that verification back once to answer it. An entry that also carries not_worth_filing is the one exception, and it is a drop rather than a decline: nothing is filed for that finding, and the accounting and the completion line say it was dropped and what the verdict said about it. It is optional because most verdicts decline nothing, and a verdict carrying none is accounted exactly as before, with every routed finding the verdict left recorded as declined without a reason.

slug.description: The slug of the routed finding being declined, as the inspection findings carry it. Matched by the accounting as the whole string, so it is the slug alone — not the file beside it, not a location — and an entry whose slug differs from the finding's by any character is recorded as though no reason was given.

reason.description: Why the finding was not corrected or repaired. Size is not among the reasons: a correct finding judged small is corrected or repaired here, where both routes cost no retry and no attempt, and one too small to be worth even those cheap routes is dropped through not_worth_filing rather than declined. The grounds that remain are that the fix is a design decision the plan did not make and no existing source settles, that the fix contradicts or is barred by something the plan does say — which wants the plan changed rather than a decision made — that a reasoned scope.do_not_modify entry protects the file where its reason speaks to the fix, or that the finding is wrong on the evidence. A choice the plan does not make that an existing source settles — a repository standard, a configured architecture document, or the way this codebase already solves the same problem — is not a reason: such a finding is recorded as repairable with a decision naming that source instead, and the coordinator's own refusal of a decision that names no source is recorded by the accounting with the refusal as its reason. A decision rides only on a repairable finding, so a fix to the words alone that needs such a choice is declined and filed all the same. A fix that is only out of the story's declared scope is not a reason either: such a finding is recorded as repairable with scope_extension instead, and the coordinator's own refusal of an extension that crosses a bound is recorded by the accounting with the bound as its reason. Written for the reader of the run who meets the accounting and wants to know why a finding reached the backlog instead of being fixed here.

not_worth_filing.description: Optional. The judgement that this correct finding is beneath what this repository files a brief at — in the severity-floor vocabulary the Inspector is given, a finding worth fixing the next time somebody has the file open rather than worth a story of its own. Its presence is the signal that the harness should drop it: nothing is filed for it, and the drop is recorded in the run's accounting beside the reason and reported in the line the run writes when it completes, so a reader sees what was dropped and why. Presence-as-signal on the terms every sibling field records: this validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so a flag with a sibling reason has a state where the flag is set and the reason is missing, while presence-as-signal has none. Write it only where the finding is correct and where neither route is worth taking — a correction and a one-file repair each cost no retry and no attempt, so size is a reason to fix rather than a reason to file, and this field is for what is smaller still. A finding you have not judged correct is not dropped through here: it is declined with the reason that it is wrong. Nothing routes on it: it decides no stage, no retry and no run status, and the drop is never inferred from the prose of a reason — only this field drops a finding.

unfinishable_by_retry.description: The verifier's judgement that no number of retries closes the gap between what remains and what an attempt delivers, together with the split it recommends between this story and a follow-on. Its presence on a failed verdict ends the run in escalation at that verification, before the retry count is compared to the ceiling: the budget is left unspent and the retry count untouched, because the judgement is that spending them would not finish the work. Its content is both the judgement and the escalation's recorded reason, so the developer reads the verifier's own words rather than a reason the coordinator composed. It is one string rather than a boolean with a sibling reason for the same limitation retry_target records above: the validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so 'reason required when the flag is true' is inexpressible, and presence-as-signal leaves no state where the signal is set and the reason is missing. It is optional because almost every verdict has no such judgement to make, and it is read only on a failed verdict — a passing verification routes nowhere, so nothing there could act on it.
